title: Architecture review: KV cache consolidation (meeting notes)
content:
Meeting: Architecture review — KV cache consolidation
Date: 2026-04-20
Time: 10:00-11:15 PT
Location: Zoom (recording on #eng-serving-runtime)
Attendees: Aisha Khan (owner), Marco Bell, Priya Desai, Ethan Liu, Zoe Martin, Lucas Grant, plus notes from offline reviewers (see linked artifacts)

Agenda:
- Quick context + goals (Aisha)
- Review options from RFC-142 and recent followups
- Tradeoffs: latency, CPU/GPU memory, network overhead, operational complexity
- Decide approach and rollout plan
- Action items and next steps

Context / problem statement:
- We currently have per-instance KV caches with inconsistent sharding logic across routes. This leads to: frequent cross-host cache misses for common prefixes, high eviction churn during rollouts, and expensive redistribution when nodes are added/removed (observed in SRV-4123).
- Goal: converge on a single consolidation strategy that: minimizes P95/P99 tail latency regressions, reduces cross-host misses for hot prefixes, stays within ops complexity and rollout safety requirements for Hosted & Dedicated modes, and plays well with our autoscaling policies and prefix/KV prefetching ideas.

Discussion notes (high level):
1) Option A — Centralized coordinator + global index
   - Idea: maintain a small global index (coordinator) that maps prefixes->shard and can be consulted on misses.
   - Pros: deterministic routing, easy to reassign prefixes, good for debugging/observability.
   - Cons: single additional component (availability/ops risk), potential latency on first lookup, scaling concerns for very high QPS.
   - Notes: Marco suggested making the coordinator soft-fail and fall back to local consistent hashing when unavailable.

2) Option B — Consistent hashing with virtual nodes (no global coordinator)
   - Idea: use consistent hashing + vnodes per instance. Rebalancing only requires moving a small set of vnodes. Add migration window to reduce hot-move churn.
   - Pros: decentralized, no extra service to operate, well-understood tradeoffs for rebalancing cost.
   - Cons: can still produce cross-host misses for skewed workloads; rebalancing still causes client-side cache warming concerns; harder to coordinate route pinning during rollouts.
   - Notes: Priya emphasized quantifying vnode count vs. observed churn using the staging replay dataset.

3) Option C — Hybrid: route-aware sharding + local consistent hash
   - Idea: first-class routing by route_id/tenant to preferred shard set; within that shard set use consistent hashing. For very hot prefixes, pin to specific nodes.
   - Pros: reduces cross-route noise, gives control for customers with SLAs, better fit for Dedicated mode where isolation matters.
   - Cons: requires more metadata and routing table management, adds complexity to routing policy layer.
   - Notes: Zoe proposed a lightweight policy DSL to express pinning and fallback; discussed tying this to rollout and canary system in Console.

4) Option D — Elastic shard reallocation + prefetch hints
   - Idea: allow elastic reallocation triggered by observed hotness; proactively prefetch top-K prefixes to new nodes during reassignments.
   - Pros: minimizes cold-start misses after reassignments, can be tuned to reduce network overhead.
   - Cons: more moving parts (metrics, thresholds, coordination), risk of prefetch overload if thresholds are noisy.

Performance/observability considerations:
- What we need to measure in staging before any rollout: cache hit rate by prefix, eviction churn rate, cross-host miss ratio, network egress bytes for KV operations, P50/P95/P99 latency for cache lookup path.
- Suggested additions to dashboards: per-route cache hit heatmaps, vnode redistribution events, rebalancing duration, and a flag to correlate rollouts to observed churn.
- Ethan will add these metrics to the staging dashboard and produce a baseline report (see action items).

Decision (consensus):
- Move forward with a phased hybrid approach that combines Option B (consistent hashing + vnodes) as the base, augmented with route-aware sharding for high-SLA tenants (Option C) and short-term coordinator-assisted rebalancing for controlled migrations (a very small-surface centralized component).
- Rationale: this balances operational simplicity (decentralized hashing) with the ability to enforce isolation and safe rollouts for Dedicated customers. The lightweight coordinator is intentionally scoped: only used for migration coordination and not on the critical lookup path (local lookup first, coordinator consulted on miss/rebalancing window).

Phased rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (prototype): implement consistent hashing + vnode library and run in staging with replay traffic. Metrics baseline collection. (Owner: Priya) — target prototype complete by 2026-05-04.
- Phase 1 (canary): enable in-hostgroup canary for a small percent of traffic in staging + internal canaries in Hosted. Monitor metrics for 1 week. (Owners: Priya + Ethan) — begin 2026-05-11.
- Phase 2 (route-aware addons): implement route-aware sharding config and pinning API for Dedicated customers; design policy DSL for pinning. (Owner: Zoe) — design doc due 2026-05-18.
- Phase 3 (coordinator + controlled migration tooling): build minimal coordinator service used only for migration orchestration and prefetch hints; ensure it is optional and fallback defaults to local consistent hashing. (Owner: Marco) — initial PR by 2026-06-01.
- Observability & safety gates: automatic rollback if P99 latency or eviction churn increases beyond configured thresholds; require signoff from SRE for Dedicated rollouts.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Priya: implement vnode-based consistent hashing library + unit tests; add feature flag to runtime to toggle new logic. Due 2026-05-04.
- Ethan: add required staging dashboards and baseline report (cache hit heatmap, eviction churn, cross-host misses). Due 2026-05-04.
- Zoe: draft design for route-aware sharding and pinning DSL; include API surface for Console. Due 2026-05-18.
- Marco: prototype coordinator service skeleton and migration protocol doc; ensure coordinator is not on the hot path. Due 2026-06-01.
- Lucas: run load/replay job for staging to produce realistic skewed prefix workload and share results with Priya/Ethan. Due 2026-04-27.
- Aisha: prepare rollout checklist and SRE safety gate definition; schedule follow-up architecture sync 2026-05-06. Due 2026-05-06.

Open questions / risks:
- How many vnodes per instance yield acceptable churn vs memory/compute overhead? (Experiment)
- Coordinator availability model: active-standby vs leaderless consensus? Keep it minimal but still HA.
- Prefetch thresholds: need careful tuning to avoid double-work / network spikes.
- Dedicated deployment differences: guarantee of tenant pinning and migration maintenance windows.

Next steps:
- Priya and Ethan to run the first staging replay and report numbers in the channel (#eng-serving-runtime).
- Follow-up sync scheduled: 2026-05-06, 10:00 PT. Agenda: review prototype metrics and confirm canary plan.

Notes / references:
- See RFC-142 for prior proposals and design tradeoffs.
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/987
- Jira ticket capturing incidents motivating this work: SRV-4123

Informal notes (things mentioned in meeting but not part of formal decision):
- We briefly discussed potential interaction with prefix/KV caching policy (LRU vs TTL hybrid). Not decided yet.
- Idea: include client-side hints in requests to help with warmup (Lucas suggested a small header to indicate recent hot prefixes).

If you have followups or disagreements with the summary above, add comments inline or ping Aisha/Marco.
